links.outcome: Lifestyle behaviours and committed action at 12 weeks, chatbot plus usual care vs usual care alone
links.effect: Modified ITT (n=460): physical activity +576 MET-min/week, fruit/vegetable intake +0.27 portions/day, committed action +0.95 a.u. versus usual care; effects sustained at 9 months; no serious adverse events.
links.quote: Modified intention-to-treat analysis (n = 460) showed significant improvements in the intervention group compared to usual care in physical activity (576 MET-min/week), fruit/vegetable intake (0.27 portions/day), and committed action (0.95 a.u.) at 12 weeks.

screen.reason: This is a pragmatic randomized controlled trial evaluating the clinical effectiveness of an automated motivational interviewing chatbot intervention for patients in primary care compared to usual care alone.
